newsitem.title: USA: US committed to liquid indexed debt market - Summers.
newsitem.headline: US committed to liquid indexed debt market - Summers.

text.p: The Treasury Department is committed to developing a large and liquid market for index-linked government securities, Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Thursday.
"I expect a liquid bond market to develop here," he told Reuters Financial Television, adding, "Obviously, it's going to take a little bit of time.'
The Treasury will hold its first sale of index-linked debt next week, $7 billion of ten-year notes to be auctioned on Jan. 29.
Summers dismissed fears that the Treasury had opted to issue index-linked debt now because of the belief that the best news on inflation is over.
"We wouldn't be issuing these bonds if we weren't confident that inflation was going to stay under control and as a consequence that taxpayers were going to realize a savings," he said.
He declined to put a precise figure on how much the Treasury might actually save, but did say it would be significant. "It's fair to say that it's in the tens of basis points," he said.
Summers defended the government's planned tax treatment of the index-linked debt, saying that it was the same as accorded more conventional U.S. Treasury securities.
"Like other bonds, these instruments will probably tend to be held in tax-favored accounts -- IRA's (Individual Retirement Accounts), 401k's (pension plans) and the like," he said.
